items.body_excerpt:
Moran comes full circle as Indigenous officers unite for historic match
Former Parramatta playmaker Dennis Moran has embraced the chance to represent his heritage as members of the NSW Police Force unite to inspire Indigenous communities across the state.
The proud Anaiwan man will lace up the boots on Saturday night when the first NSW Police Force Indigenous rugby league team takes to Allianz Stadium to take on the Royal Australian Navy Indigenous team.
The match will be played prior to South Sydney's Indigenous Round clash with Parramatta.
An Aboriginal Community Liaison Officer with the NSW Police Force in Western Sydney, Moran has seen firsthand the power of Indigenous representation within the force.
NSW Police Force Indigenous rugby league will play on Allianz Stadium on Saturday night.
So even though he retired from elite rugby league in 2008, the former playmaker is excited to return to Moore Park, 29 years after he made his first grade debut at the old Sydney Football Stadium.
"It's going to be challenging but all the boys are up for it and it's a good concept," Moran told NRL.com.
"It's a great opportunity for Aboriginal people to be exposed to our culture and to build something for the next generation. We're also showing Indigenous people that they can have fun, they get an opportunity to have a career and play football as well.
"I love being in the community and helping out. I get the opportunity to talk to families and young people in regards to things that are happening and help them make a change to become a better person, not just for themselves but for the community."
Former Eel Dennis Moran will line up for the NSW Police Indigenous team at Allianz Stadium on Saturday night.
The team has been named the Trackers to honour the historic role Indigenous people played within the NSW Police Force and has been more than 18 months in the making.
Sergeant Nathan Trueman was among the drivers of the concept and will coach the side, with former NRL players Rod Silva and Scott Mieni on the team's committee.
Joining Moran on the field on Saturday are a mix of serving officers, Aboriginal Cultural Liaison Officers and Police Force employees.
The team assembled for a three-day camp on Wednesday, with the squad conducting a number of on-field training and off-field cultural sessions.
Eels legend Dean Widders dropped in to teach the Indigenous war cry, while there will also be a community event at Redfern Oval on Thursday evening.
There will be a number of activations at the ground on Saturday, with the PCYC bringing young Indigenous kids from regional areas to Sydney for the weekend.
The team's founders are hoping Indigenous people both within and outside the force will benefit from the concept. The Trackers have allowed First Nations officers from across the state to connect, while it's also hoped the team's formation will encourage Indigenous people to join the police.
Trueman is also eager to use the team to break down some of the barriers that have historically existed between Aboriginal communities and the NSW Police Force.
Eventually, it's hoped, the Trackers will play in matches against Indigenous teams in other emergency services and even a New Zealand Māori Police team.
"Police rugby league has been around for 70 years and we've never done this before," Trueman said. "Indigenous people have been in the force since the beginning, that's where our name comes from, and this allows the police, Aboriginal people and rugby league to come together as one.
"I hope it draws more young blokes to the cops and it's a great way to break down barriers between us and the community. We've got a big community event at Redfern Oval and the boys are keen to get out in the community.
"This game will show the young blokes out there that there's people the same colour as them, the same background as them, in the police force doing good things. It opens their eyes to go, 'if he's done it, then maybe I can do it'."

NRL Casualty Ward: Panthers' Yeo blow; Tupouniua sidelined again
Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo left the field in the first half at Go Media Stadium on Friday night with a suspected pectoral injury.
Yeo went in to make a tackle and immediately reached for his shoulder and had a shocked look on his face as he reeled away.
The NSW and Australian captain left the field in the 34th minute and cut a forlorn figure on the Panthers bench in the second term. He will be sent for scans to confirm the severity of the injury.
Before the game, Panthers centre Casey McLean had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean saw three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
In Friday's second game, Roosters fullback James Tedesco missed the Round 23 blockbuster against the Bulldogs after failing to overcome an ankle injury.
Tedesco sat out the second half of the Round 22 slaughter of the Cowboys with ice on his ankle but he was initially named to return against the Bulldogs.
The skipper dropped out of the side on Thursday and has been replaced by Cody Ramsey.
However, it was another blow for Bulldogs star back-rower Sitili Tupouniua who was back from a hamstring injury, but was ruled out in his return game - again with a hamstring injury.
"Not sure how bad it is, but he's felt it in the same spot where he injured about eight weeks ago, so not ideal," Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo said after the game.
"He's pretty devastated because he was training really well and he was just excited to get back playing, this is what he does, this is what he loves doing, so he's pretty shattered."
The Knights suffered a blow ahead of Sunday's trip to Canberra with star centre Bradman Best dropping out with a calf strain suffered in last week's win over Brisbane.
Manly prop Ethan Bullemor suffered a head knock in training and will follow NRL concussion protocol. He will be stood down for 11 days meaning he will miss this week's clash against the Storm and next Friday's game against the Dolphins.
The Sea Eagles have also lost back-rower Kobe Hetherington for the remainder of the season after he suffered a ruptured bicep in training on Monday. He will undergo surgery next week.

Super Saturday in the NRL concludes with a blockbuster contest between the Rabbitohs and Eels . Returning to their spiritual home for Indigenous Round, the Rabbitohs performance holds Finals implications, and a victory will be at the forefront of their minds. The Eels are out of contention and will be playing for pride. With a bigger campaign ahead in 2027, some players are also competing for their futures. Rabbitohs vs Eels Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 23 2026
Trying hard but falling short
Outplayed in their 32-16 road loss to the Sharks last week, the Rabbitohs have several areas which need to improve should they wish to remain inside the Top 8. After a strong start which saw them score first, they soon trailed 18-6 at HT and were the inferior team in every area. With just 44% possession, they completed at 74%, they averaged 8.5m per carry and made 429 PCM’s. Their shortcomings came defensively, as they missed 51 tackles, continually allowing the Sharks to dominate the middle and create their own attacking momentum.
An ugly win is still a win
Somehow, the Eels prevailed 16-13 against the Tigers last week in an away fixture at their regular home ground. The proof of their poor execution is in the statistics. With just 45% possession, they completed at 67%, made 8.6m per carry, and had just 387 PCM’s. They were poor defensively too, missing 48 total tackles. The fact that they prevailed should be celebrated; a case can be made that the way they fought to stay in the contest should be celebrated ahead of the 2027 preseason. How they perform in this match will add or remove validity from that performance.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 17 with the Rabbitohs prevailing 32-12. They will need to draw upon that performance as they have an inferior record at this ground (32% vs 41%).
- The past 5 games have seen comfortable victories, with the average margin being 15.2 points. They have been relatively high scoring too, with the average sitting at 49.6 points.
- The Rabbitohs are the superior team on both sides of the ball in 2026. They score an average of 27ppg in attack compared to the Eels 19ppg. Defensively, they concede 24ppg compared to the Eels 28ppg.

The Rabbitohs receive a huge boost ahead of this game with Murray, Duncan, and Fifita all returning for this game. This gives them an edge over their opponents that places them in a strong position to capture victory. The Eels were horrendously bad last week and on the back of a short turnaround, they may struggle to avoid the same mistakes made. That doesn’t mean they are without a chance; 2026 has had moments whereby they have performed well, pushing teams but rarely playing for 80 minutes. If they can avoid a time limit on their performance, perhaps they will be successful.
On the other hand, the Rabbitohs have plenty of power to call upon. A positive of players returning to a team is that it strengthens their interchange. The Rabbitohs need this victory to maintain (or improve) their standing on the competition ladder. This should ensure that they are at their attacking best and pull away from their opponents late in this contest and fatigue sets in for the visitors.

NRL Team List: Round 23 v Dragons
A few changes for the Sharks ahead of their Monty Porter Memorial Cup clash with St George in the first week of Indigenous Round.
The ever-reliable Mawene Hiroti comes into the centres after a concussion to KL Iro in last Sunday's 32-16 victory over the Rabbitohs.
Iro has entered the NRL's 11-day stand-down period and will be available for selection in round 24 next week.
The Sharks are also hopeful milestone man Siosifa Talakai will be back for that home game against the Raiders, after he suffered a bicep injury on Sunday.
Jesse Colquhoun has been named to start this week, after being named on the bench the last two games but then being promoted to the starting side before kick-off each time.
Hohepa Puru returns from a concussion to take his place back on Cronulla's bench; the versatile middle forward has been a mainstay since coming into the team and impressing from round 11.
Centre Michael Gabrael has been named in jumper 18 and is a chance to make his NRL debut if called upon on Sunday.
The 21-year-old was the equal 3rd top try scorer in NSW Cup last year; Gabrael has 26 tries and 10 try assists from his 31 games for the Newtown Jets.
The Sharks will run out in the Dragons derby in their 2026 Indigenous jersey , which you can read more about HERE , with kick-off at 4:05pm at Jubilee Stadium, Kogarah.

Sharks v Titans: Ankle sidelines Kiria-Ratu; Ibrahim to debut
One of the most intriguing clashes of the round sees the Sharks host the Titans at Ocean Protect Stadium.
The Titans sit inside the top four and arrive off a gritty 18-16 win over the Warriors, while Cronulla are looking to rebound after a 32-20 loss to Wests Tigers.
Gold Coast are one of the competition's most dangerous attacking sides. Wins over the Cowboys, Eels and Warriors have demonstrated their ability to score points from anywhere on the field.
Cronulla's season has been a frustrating one, but they have shown flashes of quality, including their Round 4 win over the Raiders, but have struggled to string performances together consistently.
The battle between the halves and spine combinations could decide the outcome of this clash. While the Titans have generally looked sharper in attack, the Sharks should never be discounted.
